title: Manti Turkish Dumplings Yogurt

seo.title: Turkish Manti Recipe: Dumplings with Yogurt Sauce
seo.metaDescription: Learn to make authentic Turkish Manti, delicious tiny dumplings served with a garlicky yogurt sauce and spiced butter. This step-by-step recipe brings Turkey's favorite comfort food to your kitchen.
seo.h1: Authentic Turkish Manti Recipe: Dumplings with Yogurt Sauce
h2Headings: How to Make Turkish Manti: Step-by-Step Guide
Pro Tips for Perfect Turkish Manti
seo.imageAlt: A bowl of authentic Turkish Manti dumplings topped with garlicky yogurt sauce, spiced butter, and fresh mint.
seo.imageCaption: Savor the rich flavors of Turkey with homemade Manti, tiny beef-filled dumplings bathed in a creamy yogurt sauce and drizzled with spicy butter.

description: Manti are exquisite Turkish dumplings, tiny parcels of spiced ground beef encased in delicate dough. They are traditionally served with a rich, garlicky yogurt sauce and a vibrant drizzle of paprika-infused butter. This beloved dish offers a delightful contrast of textures and flavors, making it a true centerpiece of Turkish cuisine.

instructions.title: Prepare the Manti Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine flour and salt. Make a well in the center and add eggs and half of the water. Gradually mix, adding more water as needed, until a firm, smooth dough forms. Knead for 5-7 minutes until elastic. Cover with a damp cloth and let rest for 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Make the Filling
instructions.text: While the dough rests, combine ground beef, finely grated onion, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes in a bowl. Mix thoroughly until all ingredients are well incorporated.

instructions.title: Roll and Cut the Dough
instructions.text: Divide the rested dough into four equal pieces. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one piece very thinly (about 1/16 inch thick) into a large square or rectangle. Using a knife or pastry wheel, cut the dough into small 1-inch squares. Repeat with the remaining dough pieces.

instructions.title: Fill and Shape the Manti
instructions.text: Place a tiny pinch of the meat filling (about 1/4 teaspoon) in the center of each dough square. Bring opposite corners of the square together and pinch them firmly to seal, forming a small pyramid or boat shape. Ensure they are well sealed to prevent filling from escaping during cooking. Arrange finished manti on a floured tray.

instructions.title: Cook the Manti
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Carefully add the manti to the boiling water, stirring gently to prevent sticking. Cook for 8-10 minutes, or until the manti float to the surface and the dough is tender. Drain the manti using a slotted spoon, reserving a little cooking water if desired.

instructions.title: Prepare the Yogurt Sauce
instructions.text: While manti cooks, in a medium bowl, combine plain yogurt, minced garlic, and salt. Whisk until smooth and well combined. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.

instructions.title: Make the Spiced Butter
instructions.text: In a small saucepan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once melted and slightly bubbling, add the red pepper flakes and dried mint. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant but not burnt.

instructions.title: Serve the Manti
instructions.text: Divide the hot, drained manti among serving plates or a large communal bowl. Spoon a generous amount of the garlicky yogurt sauce over the manti. Drizzle liberally with the warm spiced butter. Garnish with fresh chopped mint or a sprinkle of sumac. Serve immediately.

tips: For truly authentic Manti, aim for very small dumplings. The smaller the better, as tradition dictates. This also ensures even cooking and a delicate texture.
Do not overfill the manti; use only a tiny amount of meat mixture, about a quarter teaspoon, to ensure they seal properly and cook thoroughly.
If you find the dough too stiff to roll thin, let it rest a bit longer. A well-rested dough is easier to work with and less likely to tear.
